# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 (Bi-Vb Pc16)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc16

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 (*Anāpucchāabhinisīdana*) is an expiation rule governing the monastic decorum of Buddhist nuns when visiting lay households. According to the rule, a nun who sits down or lies down on a seat in a house without first obtaining permission from the residents commits an offense requiring confession [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that the rule addresses instances where a nun displays undue familiarity within a lay family and disregards the courtesy and etiquette expected of a guest [Hüsken 1997].

Textually and conceptually, Pācittiya 16 forms a tight thematic cluster with the preceding rule (Pācittiya 15) and the following rule (Pācittiya 17) [Hüsken 1997]. While Pācittiya 15 deals with leaving after having sat down on a seat (*āsane nisīditvā pakkameyya*), Pācittiya 16 varies this phrasing slightly by prohibiting sitting down or lying down on a seat (*āsane abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā*) without prior authorization [Hüsken 1997].
